title: Successive derived quotients form a quotient-linear triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen coefficient universe, $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,B)$ a section whose multiplication map $B\xrightarrow{t}B$ is injective. For $j\ge1$ let $R_j=B/t^jB$ be the quotient ring sheaf. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $K\in D(B)$ put $K_j=K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R_j$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every $n>1$ there exists a distinguished triangle in $D(R_n)$
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_{n-1}}K_{n-1}\longrightarrow K_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_1}K_1\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_{n-1}}K_{n-1})[1].$$
Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is applied termwise to representing complexes. For any K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] of a representative of $K$, the first two arrows are induced by multiplication by $t$ and quotient on the second tensor factor, respectively. No boundedness or completeness assumption on $K$ is required.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient exact sequence and derived tensor triangle, retaining the R_n-action.

proof.text: Fix $n>1$. There are $R_n$-linear maps $a:R_{n-1}\to R_n$, $\bar b\mapsto\overline{tb}$, and $b:R_n\to R_1$, $\bar b\mapsto\bar b$, where the endpoint actions are restriction along the quotient ring maps. The first map is well-defined since $t(t^{n-1}c)=t^nc$; changing a lift of an $R_n$-scalar changes its action on $R_{n-1}$ by a multiple of $t^{n-1}$. Quotient sheaves have local representatives, so exactness can be checked after making such lifts on coverings, without using points. If $a(\bar c)=0$, locally $tc=t^nd$, hence $t(c-t^{n-1}d)=0$; injectivity of multiplication by $t$ gives $c=t^{n-1}d$, so $a$ is monic. If $b(\bar c)=0$, locally $c=td$, giving $\bar c=a(\bar d)$. Conversely $ba=0$, and $b$ is locally surjective by lifting a class in $R_1$ locally to $B$ and then taking its class in $R_n$. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels, as specified in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $0\to R_{n-1}\xrightarrow{a}R_n\xrightarrow{b}R_1\to0$ is short exact both as $B$-modules and as $R_n$-modules [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Second paragraph, the coefficient exact sequence; local quotient verification of its general ring-sheaf form.

proof.text: Represent $K$ by a cochain complex $G$. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to G$ with $P$ K-flat and every $P^i$ flat. No bound on $G$ is needed. For $j\in\{n-1,n,1\}$ put $C_j^i=R_j\otimes_B P^i$, with differential $1\otimes d_P^i$ and $R_j$-action on the first factor. This is a sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and a complex since $(1\otimes d_P^{i+1})(1\otimes d_P^i)=0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Regard all three complexes as $R_n$-complexes by the quotient actions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Tensor the two maps of step 1 with the identity of $P^i$ to obtain cochain maps $\alpha:C_{n-1}\to C_n$ and $\beta:C_n\to C_1$: on local pure tensors they send $\bar c\otimes p$ to $\overline{tc}\otimes p$ and $\bar c\otimes p$ to $\bar c\otimes p$. These formulas commute with $1\otimes d_P$ and are $R_n$-linear.

source.place: Tag 06YS, sites-cohomology-lemma-K-flat-resolution; termwise scalar tensor as in Tag 06YY, sites-cohomology-lemma-derived-base-change.

proof.text: For each integer $i$, flatness in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] means exactly that the sheaf functor $-\otimes_B P^i$ is exact. Apply this defining property to the $B$-module sequence of step 1. It gives $0\to C_{n-1}^i\xrightarrow{\alpha^i}C_n^i\xrightarrow{\beta^i}C_1^i\to0$ exact as $B$-module sheaves. It is exact as $R_n$-module sheaves too: by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its kernels are the same sectionwise kernels and its cokernels the same sheafified sectionwise quotients, equipped with the inherited $R_n$-actions. The kernel-image equality and zero cokernel therefore concern the very same underlying abelian sheaves. Consequently $0\to C_{n-1}\xrightarrow{\alpha}C_n\xrightarrow{\beta}C_1\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of $R_n$-complexes. This is a direct application of the exact-functor definition of flatness, not an inference from sectionwise flatness of $P^i(U)$.

source.place: Tag 03ER, sites-modules-definition-flat, item (3); Tag 03DA, sites-modules-lemma-abelian, kernels and cokernels.

proof.text: The site-size assumption makes $\operatorname{Mod}(R_n)$ abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the degreewise short exact sequence from step 3 in this category. With $Q_n$ denoting its derived localization this gives a distinguished triangle $Q_nC_{n-1}\xrightarrow{Q_n\alpha}Q_nC_n\xrightarrow{Q_n\beta}Q_nC_1\xrightarrow{\delta}(Q_nC_{n-1})[1]$ in $D(R_n)$. In particular the connecting morphism is obtained in the category of $R_n$-modules itself; no lifting of a triangle from $D(B)$ is being asserted.

For each $j$, symmetry of the sheafified balanced tensor gives an $R_j$-linear cochain isomorphism $C_j\cong P\otimes_B R_j$, sending $\bar c\otimes p$ to $p\otimes\bar c$; the inverse exchanges the factors back. The formulas respect balancing, restrictions and $1\otimes d_P$, so they extend from the presheaf tensors to their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $P\otimes_B R_j$ represents $K_j$ in $D(R_j)$ for the quotient $B\to R_j$. Termwise restriction to $R_n$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms: it retains the underlying abelian sheaf and maps [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], whose sectionwise kernels and sheafified cokernels compute cohomology [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It also commutes with the shift because it retains the differential and its negative. Thus the three objects of step 4 identify in order with $\operatorname{Res}K_{n-1},K_n,\operatorname{Res}K_1$. Under the displayed tensor exchanges, $\alpha$ becomes $p\otimes\bar c\mapsto p\otimes\overline{tc}$ and $\beta$ becomes $p\otimes\bar c\mapsto p\otimes\bar c$, exactly the required second-factor maps. Conjugate $\delta$ by these object isomorphisms and their shifts. The resulting triangle is isomorphic to step 4, hence distinguished by the definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The same construction works for any flat-term K-flat resolution, since only those two properties of $P$ were used. Neither completeness nor boundedness enters.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-2c081b581 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full: one commit, item only, no new nodes, statement verbatim from base. This is an ordinary split of Q34's statement-only node; there is no repair note for this item, and side-live still has it unsplit. All five steps are correct. Step 1: regularity of t gives injectivity of a:R_{n-1}->R_n (locally tc=t^n d gives t(c-t^{n-1}d)=0); the sequence is exact and R_n-linear using the kernel/cokernel formulas in def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category; elementary. Step 2: lem-pc-kflat-resolution gives a flat-term K-flat resolution (Stacks 06YS, sites-cohomology.tex:3207). Step 3: def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules (03ER) defines flatness as exactness of G |-> G⊗F; the item tensors R_j⊗P^i in that order, and exactness carries over to Mod(R_n) on the same abelian sheaves. Step 4: the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle applies in the abelian category Mod(R_n). Step 5: the tensor swap plus lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings(2) identify the terms with K_j; termwise restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and shifts; the triangle is distinguished as isomorphic to a cone triangle. Edge cases checked: Z with t=p and n=2, t a unit, t=0 (the regularity hypothesis is needed), unbounded K. Tool uses lem-pc-kflat-resolution and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings are accepted as generic ringed-site tools. No cycle. I searched the DAG for duplicates (successive/reduction triangles, t^{n-1} triangles) and found none. Advisory: the quotient ring sheaf B/t^jB has no definition node; this is inherited from Q34's statement.
